summary: Mauritania ended its visa on arrival on 5 January 2025: nearly all visitors now apply online for an eVisa through the official ANRPTS portal and pay the fee in cash when they land (EUR 55 for 30 days, or EUR 40 for nationals of Arab and African countries), while citizens of eleven West African and Maghreb states enter visa-free under reciprocal agreements.

primarySources.name: ANRPTS — Mauritania official e-visa and secure documents agency

defaultSource.name: Ministère des Affaires Étrangères de Mauritanie — Visa

notes: The UK government says it is illegal for Muslims and non-Muslims alike to import or consume alcohol or pork products. Baggage is scanned on arrival at Nouakchott airport and vehicles may be searched at land borders; alcohol and pork are confiscated, and people carrying them can be arrested or fined.

payments.text: The UK government says Mauritania is mainly a cash-based society: a few hotels in Nouakchott and Nouadhibou accept credit cards (some only Visa), and some ATMs accept foreign cards. US dollars and euros can be exchanged at banks, some hotels and official bureaux de change. Australia's Smartraveller adds that you must declare foreign currency on arrival and cannot leave with more than you declared.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to the east and to within 25 km of the Mali border because of terrorism risk, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest of the interior, including the southern provinces. It says crime levels are moderate but steadily increasing, with thefts and robberies at knifepoint on unlit, isolated beaches in Nouakchott.

tips.text: The UK government advises against all travel to areas within 25 km of the Malian border in the south, including Khabou, and to the east of a line through Kankossa, Akhreijit, Ghallaouia, Zouérat and Fdérik; Canada advises against all travel to northern and eastern Mauritania.
The UK government says the e-visa fee is paid on arrival in exact cash in euros or US dollars, and that change and receipts are not given. Print a copy of your e-visa to show on arrival.
The UK government advises always carrying copies of your photo ID, especially outside Nouakchott, where there are police checkpoints.

The UK government says it is illegal for anyone, Muslim or not, to import or consume alcohol in Mauritania, and Australia's Smartraveller says transporting any alcohol is also illegal unless authorised.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mauritania?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. Since January 2025 you must apply online for an eVisa through the official ANRPTS portal before travel, then pay the fee — EUR 55 for 30 days, or EUR 40 for nationals of Arab and African countries — in cash on arrival. Citizens of eleven neighboring West African and Maghreb states (including Algeria, Tunisia, Senegal and Mali) enter visa-free under reciprocal agreements; the Foreign Ministry does not state how long they may stay.

faq.question: Can I still get a Mauritania visa on arrival?
faq.answer: No. The old walk-up visa on arrival was discontinued on January 5, 2025. You must now be pre-approved online via the ANRPTS eVisa portal before boarding; the fee itself is still collected in cash at the border, together with your biometrics.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Mauritania?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

faq.question: Is Mauritania safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK government advises against all travel to areas within 25 km of the Malian border and to the east of the country, and Canada advises against all travel to northern and eastern Mauritania; Canada says there is a high risk of kidnapping and that Westerners are a preferred target.

faq.question: Can I pay by card in Mauritania?
faq.answer: Rarely. The UK government says Mauritania is mainly a cash-based society, with only a few hotels in Nouakchott and Nouadhibou accepting credit cards and some ATMs taking foreign cards, and that US dollars and euros can be exchanged at banks or official bureaux de change. Australia's Smartraveller says foreign currency must be declared on arrival.
